pages.text:
RISHIV CHHABRIA 
CE 2018-2022 
Morgan Stanley Summer Internship 
 
 
Round 1: Online Test on AMCAT (100 mins) 
Section 1: 20 mins – 10 questions: 
MCQs on PnC, statistics, puzzles (I did not attempt a few) 
Section 2: 20 mins – 7 questions 
Debugging questions with syntactical/logical errors. We could choose C/C++/Java for this 
section (passed all test cases for the majority of the questions and some for the remaining) 
Section 3: 60 mins – 3 questions 
Coding section: 
1. Find number in the given array with maximum number of 1s in its binary representation 
(passed all test cases) 
2. Based on Disjoint Set data structure (passed all test cases) 
I don’t remember the final question. 
 
Round 2: Technical (1 hr. 24 shortlisted) 
1. Compile time and run time polymorphism 
2. Difference between abstract and virtual base classes 
3. I was given a few C++ code snippets and was told to identify the error, if any, and a few 
questions related to polymorphism and inheritance related to the snippets. 
4. Given a particular scenario, I was asked how I would use inheritance and polymorphism 
to design the classes. (eg. When would you use a virtual base class and which functions 
should be declared virtual) 
5. Given a sorted array and a target sum, find 2 numbers that add up to the target. (I first 
gave the O(n^2) solution, then using a hashmap and then the 2 pointer method. In some

2 
cases, it is better to give the brute force solution first and then the optimized approach to 
the interviewer). I was told to code this and used an online compiler. 
6. Given a string, a stack and a queue, check if the string is a palindrome. (both, stack and 
queue are to be used). 
7. 2-3 SQL queries, discussion on joins, keys, and indexing. 
8. Memory layout of C program 
9. Asked if I had any questions for him (always ask a couple of questions. Can be regarding 
the projects assigned to interns, questions related to the firm, etc.) 
 
 
Round 3: Technical + Pro-Fit (45 mins. 11 shortlisted) 
1. Design a bus scheduler system (OOP based design). Basically to plan a bus route for a 
user when there are no direct buses available from the source to the destination. I was 
told to consider the bus_id, source, destination, departure_time, arrival_time, etc. Then I 
was asked to find and store the shortest distance between a few pairs of bus stops. I 
suggested using Dijkstra’s/Floyd Warshall algorithm, depending upon the use case and 
scenario. This was more of a discussion, so keep communicating your thoughts when 
such a question is asked. 
2. My experience working in a team (my views on the advantages of working in teams) 
3. How to manage an unexpected issue while working in a team, how would you split a 
reward your group receives if not everyone put in equal efforts (For these questions, try 
to give a real life scenario, eg, how did you help a teammate complete their part, etc. and 
try to slide in some quotes like “There is no I in ‘team’” :p).  
 
8 were selected for the summer internship. 
All the best!! :)
